title: Components and signs of the ordinary bounded dual and bidual
statement:
Let $(C,J,R)$ be a small ringed site with commutative coefficient sheaf under [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $E$ be a cochain complex of $R$-module sheaves, with $E^i=0$ for $i<a$ or $b<i$, where $a,b\in\mathbf Z$. Put $O=R[0]$, $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E,O)$, and $D'=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(D,O)$ using [def-pur-hom-complex], and write $T^\vee=\mathcal Hom_R(T,R)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Projection to the unique possibly nonzero factor gives canonical isomorphisms
$$D^q\cong(E^{-q})^\vee,\qquad (D')^i\cong((E^i)^\vee)^\vee.$$
Under them,
$$d_D^q(\phi)=(-1)^{q+1}\phi d_E^{-q-1},\qquad d_{D'}^i=-(d_E^i)^{\vee\vee},$$
and $D^q=0$ for $q<-b$ or $-a<q$. The homogeneous formula $x\mapsto(\phi\mapsto(-1)^{|x||\phi|}\phi(x))$ defines a chain map $\beta:E\to D'$; its degree-$i$ component, under the displayed identification, is $(-1)^i\delta_{E^i}$, where $\delta_T(t)(\phi)=\phi(t)$. These identifications and formulas hold for arbitrary $E$ with the stated bound, with no finite-free retract or exactness assumption on its terms.

proof.text: Use homComplexIsLimit and homComplexπ from [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections]. For degree q, insert into the factor p with p+q=0 using the product lift, and put zero in every other factor. Internal Hom into a zero coefficient term is zero, as follows by applying homObjMap to the zero identity. Product extensionality proves the two inverse identities. Postcompose with singleObjXSelf at degree zero to obtain α, whose hom is the specified component.

proof.text: If $q<-b$, then $-q>b$, and if $-a<q$, then $-q<a$. In either case $E^{-q}=0$ by the assumed bound. There is exactly one module-sheaf map from the zero sheaf to $R$, so [def-pur-sheaf-hom] gives $(E^{-q})^\vee=0$. Step 1 gives $D^q=0$. This also covers $a>b$, when every $E^p$ is zero.

proof.text: Apply homComplex_d_π of [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections] with arbitrary adjacent n,m and surviving source indices p,p′. The target differential of R[0] is zero, so only negative (-1)^n times precomposition survives. Postcomposition with singleObjXSelf commutes with precomposition by homObjMap_comp_homObjMap. Since m=n+1 this is (-1)^m times precomposition, giving the stated differential equation.

proof.text: Construct γ as α for the dual complex followed by contravariant internal Hom of the inverse of α for E. Functoriality and the inverse identities give the required projection square. Apply the first differential formula both to E and its dual. Transport the formula for the dual differential through α inverse. Internal Hom is additive in its source, so its precomposition map carries integer unit scalars to the same scalars. The product of the two signs is (-1)^(i+1)(-1)^i=-1. Contravariant composition gives the negative double transpose.

proof.text: The size convention makes C essentially small in max(c,v,r). Use coefficientSheafification from [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-pullback-exists-universes] and the standard derived-category instance to instantiate the already proved ringedSiteOrdinaryBidual_existsUnique from [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. Its β is an actual chain map with the signed slice evaluation formula in coefficient degree zero. Define δ^i=(-1)^i β^i γ_i. To check ordinary evaluation, evaluate this composite on a functional transported by α inverse. The product of signs (-1)^i(-1)^(i*(-i)) is one, and α inverse followed by α cancels, leaving φ(x restricted to the slice). This proves the required section formula for δ without any reflexivity assumption.

proof.text: The β obtained in step 5 is already a chain map. Its defining RingedSiteBidualFormula gives the homogeneous formula when t=0. When t≠0, the coefficient term of R[0] is zero; evaluating its zero identity shows every section is zero, so both sides of the formula belong to a subsingleton section module and are equal. Finally (-1)^i δ^i=β^i γ_i since the square of an integer unit is one. Assemble these equations with steps 1–4 and the support bound from step 2.
